paper_diagnosis: Invasive aspergillosis involving the lungs and brain after short period of steroid injection
disease_label_per_paper: Invasive aspergillosis involving the lungs and brain after intra-articular corticosteroid injections
paper_diagnosis_source_text_value: Here, we report an invasive aspergillosis case, which involves the lungs and brain after a short period of steroid injection.
presentation_summary: Two weeks of general weakness and poor oral intake after two months of weekly bilateral intra-articular triamcinolone injections.
Admission showed low-grade fever, acute ill appearance, sleepiness, oral mucosal ulcers with whitish patches, and diffuse mild crackles.
Labs showed leukocytosis with marked neutrophilia, lymphopenia, hypoalbuminemia, elevated CRP, hyperglycemia, and HbA1c 7.7%.
Chest radiograph and CT showed multiple bilateral cavitary pulmonary nodules and masses.
Percutaneous lung biopsy showed acute-angle branching fungal hyphae; later MRI showed multiple brain lesions, and the patient died of respiratory failure and septic shock.
